purpose: Retrieve or locate the authoritative text of the provision this workspace implements for CRP-LSRC-0362, recording source identity, applicable edition and relevant application context, so that the implemented reliability concern can be checked against the provision's own wording rather than against its legacy rule name or an unrecorded gloss.
authority_basis: The owner instruction for this batch: complete a bounded legal-attribution and presentation check (provision text, attribution, one coherent consumer issue, temporal applicability, selected/downloaded content).

WORKSPACE AGENTS.md: CRP identifies compliance violations and probable violations from recorded rules and source-linked report evidence with specific uncertainty; the legacy rule name is not a substitute for the provision's wording.

section_9_structure_located.basis: the authoritative consolidated index (CanLII, RSO 1990, c C.33) and the e-Laws table of contents for the same Act
section_9_structure_located.significance: s. 9(2) and 9(3) are the subsections that govern what a consumer report may INCLUDE. s. 9(3)(a) sits inside that list, not inside a retention or timing provision.

located_provision_text.quoted_subsection_lead_in: 9(3) A consumer reporting agency shall not include in a consumer report,
located_provision_text.quoted_paragraph_a: (a) any credit information based on evidence that is not the best evidence reasonably available;
located_provision_text.quoted_paragraph_b: (b) any unfavourable personal information unless it has made reasonable efforts to corroborate the evidence on which the personal information is based, and the lack of corroboration is noted with and accompanies the information;
located_provision_text.why_these_are_quoted: The implemented rule is a CONTENT rule. Its attribution to s. 9(3)(a) may only be recorded against the provision's own words, so the words are recorded here and carried into the rule's recorded subject, its limb and its consumer wording.

attribution_check.implemented_concern: an ordinary account whose printed opened date is later than its printed closed date: the report's own two printed values for that single account cannot both be right
attribution_check.provision_concern: s. 9(3)(a) prohibits including in a consumer report any credit information based on evidence that is not the best evidence reasonably available
attribution_check.basis: If the best evidence reasonably available for one account had been relied on, that account's own printed opened and closed values would agree. Values that cannot both be right are therefore affirmative evidence, still rebuttable, that the credit information included for that account was not based on the best evidence reasonably available. The provision speaks to the evidence basis of included credit information, and a transcription or update error that leaves a printed value unfaithful to the best available evidence falls inside the same limb, so the mapping holds on either reading.
attribution_check.confidence_ceiling_justified: PROBABLE_VIOLATION. The report establishes the conflict between its own values; it establishes neither which value is unreliable nor whether a benign explanation applies. A VIOLATION ceiling remains refused, not downgraded.
scope_limits_recorded: the limb is confined to CREDIT information: this rule runs only on an ordinary credit account record (record kind CONSUMER_CREDIT_LIABILITY) and never on personal information, so the companion personal-information limb of the same subsection is not invoked

the Act's own definition of 'credit information' enumerates kinds of information about a consumer (for example paying habits and outstanding debt obligations) and does not name account dates expressly; the rule therefore rests on the account's dates being information about the consumer's debt obligation, and that reading is recorded here as a stated interpretive limit rather than presented as settled
no exception recorded in the located text is evaluated, and off-report knowledge (a furnisher's own records) is never inferred

corrected_recorded_subject.previous_recording_defect: the rule's recorded subject previously read 'information that is not based on the most reliable evidence reasonably available'. That phrasing is not this provision's. It is a gloss on the phrase used by a different Canadian instrument, and it was substituted for the provision's own wording.
corrected_recorded_subject.corrected_subject: a consumer reporting agency shall not include in a consumer report any credit information based on evidence that is not the best evidence reasonably available (Consumer Reporting Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. C.33, s. 9(3)(a))
corrected_recorded_subject.consequence: the gloss is replaced everywhere it was recorded — the adapter limb, the adapter exceptions basis, the finding gate, the runtime comments, the consumer wording and the disposition record. The adapter id and the legacy rule id are internal keys and are preserved unchanged, because provenance and internal classification are not rewritten by a wording correction.

temporal_applicability.what_is_recorded: the consolidation period of the applicable edition (from July 1, 2026 to the e-Laws currency date), its last amendment (2025, c. 24, Sched. 6), and that the last amendment does not touch section 9
temporal_applicability.what_is_not_recorded: the commencement date of the R.S.O. 1990 revision or of s. 9(3)(a), and any historical version list for the provision
temporal_applicability.corrected_earlier_assertion: An earlier statement in this workspace said that no effective date was needed because the rule counts no period and performs no arithmetic against a reference date. That was wrong. Temporal applicability is a condition of LEGAL ATTRIBUTION for every rule, including a content rule: a provision must be in force, and the version applied must be the one governing the report's period, before the provision can be named against a report. It is a different question from retention arithmetic, which this rule does not perform (it counts no period, applies no day offset and ages nothing). The two are kept apart here: the arithmetic claim is true, the applicability claim is not made.
how_the_rule_keeps_this_honest: the rule emits no period-based conclusion and states no retention period
the rule's recorded edition is the consolidation in force, recorded with its period and last amendment
the rule claims no commencement date, and the absence of one is recorded as a retained limitation rather than assumed away

consumer_presentation_outcome.attribution: RETAINED as a qualified probable issue: the provision supports the assessment, so the statutory attribution and the statutory coverage claim are kept, with the provision's own wording recorded and the specific uncertainty stated
consumer_presentation_outcome.specific_uncertainty_retained: which of the two printed values is unreliable is not established by the report, and a benign explanation (a later correction of one date, or an account reopened after it was closed) may exist
consumer_presentation_outcome.one_coherent_issue: the same printed conflict previously reached the consumer twice — once as the shared factual observation and once as the Ontario probable issue. They are now presented as ONE issue carrying both supported bases (the factual conflict the report prints, and the recorded Ontario rule it raises) with ONE verification request. Internal classifications, provenance and source locations are preserved inside the issue.
consumer_presentation_outcome.request_type: VERIFICATION, never a correction demand: what the report shows is a probable reporting issue to verify, not an established violation
